business_scope.primary_industry_name: Direct Online Retail of Portable Battery Generators and Solar Panels

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified, non-religious; with regional foral laws in limited areas)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU-Singapore Investment Protection Agreement (2021, applicable to Spain)
EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement (investment provisions applicable to Spain)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended by Real Decreto-ley 7/2021 and transposing EU AML Directives 4 and 5; Royal Decree 304/2014 (Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010); Royal Decree 171/2023 on the ultimate beneficial ownership register; Circular 1/2017 of SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or current registry extract of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction (e.g., Companies House, local Registro Mercantil)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention 5-Oct-1961) plus sworn Spanish translation; consular legalization is not required when the issuing state is party to the Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special or General Power of Attorney granted to the incorporators
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the shareholder's jurisdiction or Spanish consulate in the shareholder's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization in non-Apostille states) followed by sworn translation into Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of address of each director, manager and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority of the individual's origin (police, notary, or registry) / official translator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification with Hague Apostille and sworn translation into Spanish; Spanish NIE/TIE obtained for non-resident managers

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory preventive screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs and authorized agents against PEP lists maintained by SEPBLAC, OFAC SDN, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List and Spanish domestic sanction lists. Any PEP detection requires enhanced due diligence under Article 14 of Ley 10/2010, including source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation. Screening results must be retained for a minimum of 10 years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central - Certificación de Denominación Social / Sede Electrónica (Colegio de Registradores de España, www.registradores.org)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be submitted in Spanish; Catalan, Galician or Basque words are admissible if transcribed in Spanish script. Foreign names are permitted when transliterated into the Spanish alphabet and accompanied by a sworn Spanish translation ensuring phonetic distinction and compatibility with Spanish naming principles. Names may not contain logos, vulgar phrases, false trademarks or references to public authorities.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco / Caja / Financiera (requires Bank of Spain authorization)
Sociedad Anónima / S.A. (misleading, not permitted for SL)
Unión Europea / Organización Mundial / Naciones Unidas
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: When the name is denied, the online application will be returned with an automatic certificate of denial; the applicant may file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) with the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado (DGRN) within one month of notification, and may simultaneously reserve a new denomination online. Valid names are granted a certification of non-registration (certificación negativa de denominación social) valid for 90 days; an extension may be requested in the 15-day period before expiration, giving a further 90 days maximum before the certificate expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is admissible for receiving correspondence and for registration purposes, provided it is a real Spanish postal address. However, the SL must maintain a center of effective management in Spain for corporate law purposes. For online retail of solar generators, if the company holds inventory in a Spanish warehouse or fulfills orders from Spain, SEPBLAC and the State Tax Agency (AEAT) may treat the virtual office as insufficient commercial substance, so a physical office or fulfilment center should be engaged via a contractual service provider.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced on-site inspection: low to moderate (approximately 15-20% annual probability for a new e-commerce SL with a virtual office and ERP setup), rising to 30-35% if the company is registered for VAT and carries stock or conducts order fulfilment in Spain. AEAT and SEPBLAC perform risk-based inspections focusing on UBO accuracy, economic substance and invoice triangulation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial authorization of the incorporation deed (escritura pública) and company bylaws

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff (Royal Decree 1426/1989, based on registered capital and number of pages)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Provisional registration of the SL and submission at the local Mercantile Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registry tariff (Real Decreto 1417/2004 and DGRN scales; depends on capital amount)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille legalization of foreign corporate documents and sworn Spanish translation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish sworn translator (traductor jurado) and foreign notary / competent authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for sworn translation (€60-120 per document) plus apostille issuance fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Non-resident identification number (NIE) application fees for foreign directors

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Virtual registered office address subscription (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark prevailing rate for a virtual office address with document handling in Spain

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/UBO register onboarding and due diligence package (notarial opening of UBO file and SEPBLAC pre-assessment)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; fixed fee for corporate due diligence plus applicable notary costs for UBO disclosure

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), Articles 20-31 (constitution), 72-92 (S.L. capital and shares), and 107-109 (registered office).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (for name certificates) and the provincial Registro Mercantil of the province where the registered office is established.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura pública de constitución (public deed of incorporation), executed before a Spanish notary and thereafter inscribed in the Mercantile Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: A Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may be formed with minimum share capital of EUR 3,000 (approximately USD 3,260), fully subscribed and fully paid in cash or in-kind. Alternatively, an SL de Formación Sucesiva may be formed with capital below EUR 3,000 provided that only up to 20% of distributable profits is allocated to reserves and certain statutory limitations apply. The capital contribution must be deposited in a Spanish credit institution or Banco de España account in the company's name before execution of the deed; the deposit can be released only after registration of the company in the Mercantile Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: In accordance with the articles of incorporation, the sole founding shareholder adopts the following resolutions: 1. The share capital is duly subscribed and fully paid in cash, as evidenced by the bank certificate of deposit filed with the preliminary notarial protocol. 2. The registered office of the company is fixed at [address], municipality, province, Spain. 3. The management of the company is entrusted to the designated sole administrator, who accepts the appointment and exercises all legal powers. 4. The administrator is authorized to execute public deeds, sign declarations before the Commercial Registry, obtain tax identification numbers, and complete the opening of bank accounts. 5. All necessary filings with the Commercial Registry and regulatory agencies are hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain certification of corporate name availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, via the online portal servicio de certificación de denominación social
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a reservation request for the proposed company name using Form S-1. The request must identify up to three alternative names. The name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación) is issued online and has a maximum validity of three months, which must be sufficient to execute the deed. Submit legalized identification of shareholders and administrators.
required_dossiers: Application form for negative name certificate
Copy of passport or DNI/NIE of each founding shareholder
Power of attorney if a representative acts
Description of intended corporate name and alternatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity or reserved name, submit a new application within the same protocol listing different alternatives and, if necessary, file an administrative appeal before the Directorate General of Legal Certainty and Public Faith (DGSJFP).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a preliminary bank account and deposit share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any Spanish credit institution or Banco de España authorized to hold deposit guarantees
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a bank account in the name of the company in formation and deposit the minimum capital amount. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit or negative balance certificate expressly stating that the amount is at the company's disposal and blocked until the Mercantile Register inscription is presented. For in-kind contributions, obtain a statutory valuation report from an expert unless all members agree otherwise under Article 73 LSC.
required_dossiers: Name certificate from the Mercantile Register
Draft articles of association
NIE of each shareholder or administrator
Passport or identity documents
Proof of lawful source of the deposited funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue the certificate, verify the legal identity of the company in formation and the identifiers; correct the file and request a replacement certificate. In case of regulatory non-compliance, apply to the Bank of Spain for a formal ruling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the incorporation deed before a notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary of the registral district where the registered office will be located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Summon all founding shareholders or their duly empowered attorneys before the notary. The notary will verify legal capacity, the certificate of name, the deposit certificate, the in-kind valuation report where applicable, and the statutory clauses. Sign the Escritura pública de constitución and obtain the first authenticated copies for filings.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate
Bilateral agreement or draft bylaws
Report of experts or auditors for in-kind contributions (if any)
Identity documents and NIE of all shareholders
Statement of designated registered office and administration structure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises formal defects, correct the deed by executed acta or new escritura, obtaining the notary's validation of the amended clauses before proceeding to registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for provisional taxpayer identification number (NIF provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), local tax office or online at sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after signing the deed, submit Modelo 036 declaring the beginning of activity and applying for irreversible provisional NIF. Provide a certified copy of the public deed and the notary's certificate that the application was filed before registration. The provisional NIF facilitates bank account activation and later registration filings.
required_dossiers: Modelo 036 form
Certified first copy of the escritura de constitución
Notary's certification of presentation of NIF application
Dossier of all shareholders and administrators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT rejects the application because the activity code is inconsistent, amend the attached acts and resubmit Modelo 036 with the correct IAE/ISIC code (4791 retail sale via internet), and correct any pending personal tax identification numbers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscribe the company in the Mercantile Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Registro Mercantil of the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the first certified copy of the deed together with the Modelo 036 receipt, proof of provisional NIF, and the bank certificate of capital deposit with the Mercantile Register. The registrar verifies legal compliance and issues a registration entry. Upon inscription, the company acquires legal personality and the capital deposit may be released.
required_dossiers: First certified copy of the notarial deed
Copy of provisional NIF certificate
Bank certificate of capital deposit
Certification of the notary that the deed is within legal limits
If applicable, prior authorization reports
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a deficiency note (nota de defectos), correct the indicated defects by supplementary deed or amend the statutes, then resubmit the dose. If the registry denies inscription, file an appeal before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within two months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain definitive NIF and post-registration municipal environmental or activity clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and municipal council of the registered office/warehouse location
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the incorporation is registered, apply to the AEAT for the definitive NIF (CIF) by presenting the certificate of registration with the Mercantile Register. Concurrently submit a Declaración responsable de inicio de actividad or, if any physical premises are leased or owned, a municipal environmental activity license if required under local ordinances. Then notify the AEAT and the Social Security treasury of the definitive registry data.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration from the Mercantile Register
Modelo 036 with definitive NIF request
Municipal activity license or declaration responsible
Proof of occupational risk assessment and building installation compliance
WEEE register and packaging registration certificates if selling portable electrical equipment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT or municipality suspends the procedure due to incomplete documentation or activity mismatch, promptly supply the corrected forms and pay any applicable fee. If the municipal denial is based on zoning incompatibility, submit an urban planning certificate from the official municipal architect or file an administrative appeal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Generalitat regional industrial administration / Spanish Ministry of Industry and Tourism (Dirección General de Industria y de la Pequeña y Mediana Empresa), acting jointly with the municipal licensing department for retail premises and e-commerce logistics centers.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de apertura o declaración responsable de inicio de actividad (municipal activity opening license/responsible declaration) for warehousing, showroom, and direct online retail of portable battery generators and solar panels.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico, Dirección General de Calidad y Evaluación Ambiental, or the regional environmental authority (Comunidad Autónoma), depending on the physical storage capacity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not subject to EIA for online retail and low-scale warehousing; only an environmental activity registration or municipal environmental communication is required for storage facilities of modest floor area, except when the site exceeds Annex thresholds of Law 21/2013 on environmental assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater is generated; compliance is required with Royal Decree 102/2011 on air quality, Royal Decree 1055/2022 on packaging waste, Royal Decree 110/2015 on electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) reporting, and with municipal ordinances for waste collection and stormwater. Volatile organic compound emissions from battery and solar panel storage are negligible; battery waste handling must comply with Royal Decree 110/2015 and Regulation (EU) 2023/1542.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under Royal Decree 2267/2004 for industrial establishments, including portable extinguishers and emergency exits; structural load inspection and electrical certificate (boletín eléctrico) from a competent authorized installer; occupational risk prevention plan under Law 31/1995 and Royal Decree 486/1997 on workplace safety; and, if the premises open to the public, accessibility clearance under Royal Decree 505/2007.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); online portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL): (1) execute the public deed of incorporation before a notary; (2) obtain a provisional corporate NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal, format B+7 digits+control character) from AEAT via Form 036 prior to registration; (3) register the company at the Registro Mercantil; (4) file Form 036 for the definitive NIF and simultaneous enrolment in the Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores, which constitutes mandatory Spanish VAT (IVA) census registration — Spain imposes no turnover threshold; (5) obtain an AEAT electronic certificate for online filing, SII submissions and customs e-export procedures; (6) if the SL makes distance sales to consumers in other EU Member States, register in the Spanish Union OSS portal, and register under Import OSS/IOSS if importing low-value consignments for onward sale; (7) obtain digital certificates for the electronic Single Administrative Document (DUA) filings. A resident SL requires no Spanish fiscal representative, but a non-resident entity without a permanent establishment selling into Spain must appoint one.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the SL is a separate legal person and full taxpayer for Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Corporate Income Tax, Ley 27/2014) on worldwide income; general CIT rate 25%; newly created entities benefit from a 15% rate for the first two tax periods with a positive taxable base (art. 29.3 LIS); a 23% reduced rate applies to entities with net turnover below EUR 1,000,000 for tax periods 2023-2024, subject to extension; no pass-through/check-the-box eligibility; outbound dividends are subject to 19% non-resident withholding generally, 0% for qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive parents and lower treaty rates elsewhere.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no elective check-the-box classification. Available elections: (1) optional consolidated tax group regime under arts. 61-77 LIS for groups with 75% or greater control; (2) ETVE (Entidad de Tenencia de Valores Extranjeros) holding-company election for foreign-source dividends and capital gains relief; (3) reduced-dimension entity election for the 23% small-entity rate; (4) merger/demerger tax-neutrality option under art. 89.3 LIS; (5) hybrid mismatch treatment under art. 15 bis LIS (ATAD) is mandatory rather than elective, disallowing deductions or requiring inclusion to neutralise hybrid mismatches, with an optional switch-over adjustment in certain double-dip arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido) — Spanish VAT harmonised with Directive 2006/112/EC; peninsular Spain and the Balearic Islands apply national IVA, while the Canary Islands (IGIC), Ceuta and Melilla (IPSI) operate separate territorial regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold: any taxable person supplying goods or services in peninsular Spain or the Balearic Islands must register for IVA from commencement of activity. For non-established EU traders, the former EUR 35,000 distance-sales threshold is replaced by the EUR 10,000 Union-wide OSS threshold; below EUR 10,000, distance sales remain taxable in the seller's EU state unless fulfilled from a Spanish warehouse. Imported low-value consignments up to EUR 150 may benefit from import VAT exemption with VAT collected at destination via IOSS. Small retailer regimes: 'régimen simplificado' and 'recargo de equivalencia' apply to retail trade with annual turnover not exceeding EUR 1,000,000; the recargo de equivalencia obliges the supplier to charge a 5.2% / 1.4% / 0.5% surcharge by rate category and the retailer may not deduct input VAT on purchases.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información del IVA) is mandatory for entities with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6,000,000, for those in consolidated VAT groups, and for exporters applying the monthly refund regime; it requires API-based XML transmission of all invoice records to AEAT within 8 calendar days of invoice issuance or accounting record, replacing aggregate periodic returns for covered transactions. Under Ley 18/2022 ('Crea y Crece') and the enabling Royal Decree adopted in December 2024, mandatory B2B e-invoicing is phased in for all operators: companies with turnover above EUR 8,000,000 within one year, all others within two years; e-invoices must use interoperable formats (Facturae, UBL 2.1, CII) generated by verified software satisfying Veri*factura anti-fraud standards, with a machine-readable QR code requirement pending the technical ministerial order.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically dispatched or transported by the seller, or by a third party on its behalf, to a destination outside EU customs territory qualify for the exemption with credit (0% IVA) under art. 21 LIVA (Ley 37/1992), including portable solar power and battery products sold through e-commerce. Intra-EU B2B supplies to a taxable person in another Member State are exempt under art. 25 LIVA subject to a valid customer VAT number and Intrastat compliance. B2B services supplied to third-country recipients fall outside Spanish VAT scope under art. 69 LIVA with input VAT recoverable. Direct B2C distance sales to EU consumers are not zero-rated; they are taxed at the destination Member State rate through the Spanish Union OSS portal. Solar portable power equipment is not subject to Spanish excise duties; import VAT and duties in the destination non-EU country are borne by the consumer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — DUA/e-Export Single Administrative Document filed through Spanish Customs (AES electronic export system)
Transport document: Bill of Lading for sea freight, Air Waybill for air freight, or CMR consignment note for road freight destined outside the EU
Proof of physical exit from EU customs territory: carrier movement tracking, AEAT exit confirmation, or third-country customs entry records
E-commerce transactional evidence: customer order record, Stripe/acquiring payment confirmation, and shipping label evidencing non-EU consignee address
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/card settlement record evidencing collection of the export consideration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT audits export zero-rating strictly against physical exit evidence; failure to substantiate departure triggers reversal of the 0% rate and assessment of output IVA on the sale price. The VAT clawback limitation period is 4 years (arts. 66-67 LGT), extended in cases of concealment. Sanctions under art. 191 LGT: penalty of 50% of the VAT evaded, increased to 100% for methodical concealment and 150% for obstruction or fraudulent invoicing, plus statutory arrears interest (interés de demora, 4.0625% in 2025); joint and several liability may attach to acquirers or intermediaries participating in export fraud. Exporters registered in SII may claim monthly IVA refunds under the special monthly refund regime (art. 30.3 RD 1624/1992), which is subject to heightened documentary scrutiny. Spain does not impose a statutory foreign-currency repatriation deadline for export zero-rating; the 180-day benchmark is retained as an internal documentary-coherence standard.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem; external-transaction and balance-of-payments oversight jointly administered by the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio (Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones, Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa); AML/CFT FIU is SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias). Core legal instruments: Real Decreto 1816/1991 (economic transactions with the exterior), Ley 10/2010 (AML/CFT), Ley 21/2011 (electronic money), RDL 5/2023 (foreign investment screening), and RDL 5/2004 (non-resident income tax on remittances).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full de jure and de facto convertibility of EUR on both current and capital account under Articles 63-66 TFEU; no exchange controls, prior authorizations, or rationing apply to payments, transfers, or profit remittances. An SL may distribute dividends to non-resident shareholders at any time, subject only to Non-Resident Income Tax withholding (19% statutory, typically 5-15% under DTTs) and standard corporate formalities. Capital-account operations (foreign direct investment, shareholder loans) require only ex-post statistical declarations; prior filing or authorization is triggered solely for (i) operations equal to or exceeding the RD 1816/1991 individual declaration threshold (in practice EUR 12,500 per operation, as updated by implementing ministerial orders), reported electronically through the executing bank, and (ii) investments by non-EU/EFTA residents in critical sectors enumerated by RDL 5/2023 (defence, dual-use goods, critical infrastructure, data, media, energy, transport), which do not include online retail of portable power. E-commerce receipts collected through Stripe-style PSPs are aggregated by the PSP and the settlement bank, eliminating per-transaction balance-of-payments filings; cross-border merchant collections are freely credited to Spanish EUR accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None apply. Spain imposes no surrender, mandatory conversion, repatriation, or holding-period requirements on export proceeds; the SL may retain EUR or foreign currency domestically or abroad at its discretion. For statistical integrity under RD 1816/1991, export and online-sales collections equal to or exceeding EUR 12,500 per operation must flow through authorized banking channels and be annotated with the correct balance-of-payments statistical business purpose code (e.g., online retail sale of merchandise); the executing bank files the declaration. No compulsory export credit insurance or hedging mandate exists; CESCE and ICO facilities are optional commercial tools.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Cuenta de Depósito / certificación de capital) and Cuenta Corriente Empresarial (operational EUR account); strong international trade desk supporting LatAm corridors.
Capital Escrow Account and Exprés Empresas operational account; open-architecture PSP/acquiring integrations; BBVA Spark startup unit for tech e-commerce.
Capital Escrow Account and Cuenta Negocios / Comercio Electrónico operational account; strongest merchant-acquiring franchise in Spain (Comercia/Paytpv ecosystem).
Capital Escrow Account and B100 digital operational account (fully remote onboarding for EEA-resident directors); solid SME trade finance.
Capital Escrow Account and Cuenta In/Out operational account; premium service but tighter risk appetite for high-velocity online-only retail.
Capital Escrow Account and Cuenta Negocios operational account; adequate niche alternative with regional onboarding latency.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium-High as an overlay treasury rail; Low as the sole banking backbone. EU-licensed EMIs/PSPs (Revolut, Wise, Qonto; the Irish entity of Stripe for settlement) may passport into Spain under PSD2 and Ley 21/2011 and lawfully hold corporate funds and execute SEPA/SWIFT flows; non-EEA EMIs cannot. Hard limits: EMIs offer no Spanish Deposit Guarantee Fund coverage, generally cannot issue the notarial certificado de depósito required for standard SL capital formation, and may reject the bank reference needed at incorporation. Note that the BNPL rail 'Affirm' is not licensed or passported in Spain; use Klarna, SeQura, or BBVA's Aplazame for equivalent split-payment rails. Blueprint: maintain a Tier-1 licensed bank for statutory capital, escrow certification, and clearing, plus Wise Business (multi-currency FX, CNY/USD payables) and Stripe settlement flows as non-deposit-taking overlay rails for e-commerce liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under Ley 10/2010 and Banco de España Circular 2/2018, legal representatives, directors, and UBOs must be positively identified. Remote onboarding is legally admissible when an eIDAS-notified electronic ID or supervised video identification is used, and is in practice accepted by digital arms (Openbank, Sabadell B100) for EEA-resident directors; however, the branch-based underwriting of the six Tier-1 banks de facto mandates at least one physical appearance of the administrator or of a Spanish-resident legal representative (apoderado) holding a valid NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) and a notarized, apostilled power of attorney. Non-EU directors (LatAm parent chain) must additionally present: escritura de constitución (notarized and apostilled), a current certificación del Registro Mercantil, the UBO declaration, a board resolution appointing signatories, proof of address and tax residence of the company, a source-of-funds report, and they must pass an in-person or official video KYC interview with a compliance officer. Budget 3-6 weeks for first account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity, sub-EUR 50 B2C card receipts from SEPA and global markets running over the declared business profile, alongside supplier wires to manufacturing counterparties in the PRC - a classic e-commerce money-laundering profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized escritura de constitución and CIF certificate; positive Registry certification identifying directors and UBOs; Stripe settlement reports reconciled to a sample of dated customer orders with tracking IDs; supply contracts and pro-forma invoices from PRC vendors with Incoterms; customs entry (DUI/SAD) attesting goods import and EU warehouse flow; projected or first-year annual accounts; completed AML questionnaire; signed undertaking to onboard no third-party funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque multi-tier UBO chain (non-EU holding vehicle in a high-risk jurisdiction such as Panama, BVI, Seychelles, or Cayman) or a PEP-linked ultimate owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full organic chart (100% chain) with share registers; apostilled certificate of good standing and constitutional documents of each vehicle; tax-residence certificates of all UBOs; written commercial explanation of the LatAm bridge rationale; NIE and Spanish tax clearance certificates of the appointed administrators; separation undertaking between shareholder loans and capital contributions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Elevated chargeback or refund ratios, or acquiring-risk scoring caused by BNPL split payments and consumer-law return abuse on portable battery products.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Published refund and returns policy with LSSI-CE compliant website terms; Stripe chargeback ratio report maintained under 0.5%; dispute-resolution logs; proof-of-delivery records for contested shipments; merchant monitoring registration acceptable to SEPBLAC; acquiring agreement from an authorized EU payment institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large one-off inbound wires (capital injection or settlement spike) breaching the bank's turnover expectation, or counterparties touched by EU/UN sanctions screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board minutes approving the capital increase and bank details; notarial escritura for the capital operation; source-of-funds statements (3-month bank statements at shareholder level); financing agreement for any shareholder loan at market rate; sanctions-screening confirmation against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list and UN list; declaration under Ley 10/2010 for any cash-related funds above EUR 10,000; pre-notification to the compliance officer prior to large deposits.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Standard SL incorporation requires a notarial certificate of capital deposit (certificado de depósito) evidencing minimum capital of EUR 3,000 under the TRLSC, unless the flexible Sociedad de Formación Sucesiva regime (Ley 18/2022) is used (formation from EUR 1 with a legal reserve flag). Inbound shareholder remittance: SWIFT MT103 (non-SEPA shareholders) or SEPA Credit Transfer in ISO 20022 pain.001 (EU shareholders), instructing the beneficiary CIF/NIE of the SL, with purpose code 32101 (préstamo) for loans or capital-contribution wording in field 70 such as 'Aportacion de capital social - escritura [notary name/no.] - fecha'; for operations equal to or above EUR 12,500, the bank files the RD 1816/1991 statistical declaration. Non-EU investors completing foreign direct investment must file the statistical post-declaration with the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio (electronic registry), and where the investor is resident outside the EU/EFTA, verify inapplicability of the RDL 5/2023 screening (not triggered for portable-power retail). Stripe e-commerce receipts settle as aggregated SEPA payouts from the Irish PSP entity rather than as individual client transfers; disclose the acquiring agreement to the bank and ensure PSP settlement codes appear in the accounts. For BNPL, Affirm is not licensed or passported in Spain; route split payments through Klarna, SeQura, or Aplazame to maintain compliance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments within SEPA execute via SEPA Credit Transfer (instant SCT Inst available) with VAT reverse-charge treatment noted; non-EU trade (PRC solar-module suppliers, USD or CNY invoicing) executes via SWIFT MT103 direct or MT103 cover. For recurring bulk orders above approximately USD 500,000, use an irrevocable import Letter of Credit (UCP 600) at sight or 90-day usance confirmed by a Chinese advising bank; a documentary collection (CAD) suits smaller flows. MT799 pre-advices support large LC issuance. Multi-beneficiary payouts to PRC suppliers should run through the bank's payment-factory channel (e.g., Santander Trade product suite, BBVA Trade Solutions, CaixaBank Global Payments) using SWIFT FileAct; each instruction must carry accurate field 70 remittance information (e.g., 'Importacion modulos solares - factura #XXXX') so that goods-flow customs entries (DUI/AEO) match the payment audit trail. Refund disbursements must loop exclusively through the originating PSP API rails rather than mass SEPA transfers, and CNY-payable FX conversion should be executed by the treasury desk at the point of disbursement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable FX forward contracts (tenor up to 12 months) - vanilla instruments documented under ISDA 2002 or the Spanish CMOF (Contrato Marco de Operaciones Financieras)
EUR/CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) settled in EUR against the CNH reference fix - permissible for hedging PRC import payables without CNY deliverability in Spain
FX swaps (spot-to-forward or forward-to-forward rollovers) for managing settlement-date mismatches
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) - permissible only for asset-linked capex or external borrowing with notional generally above EUR 5 million; practically unavailable for an early-stage SL
Plain vanilla FX options (collars, zero-cost collars, participating forwards) - permitted with standard house documentation
EURIBOR-indexed interest rate swaps to hedge floating-rate import financing - optional and subject to EMIR reporting and margin rules

Prohibited or non-advised without special authorization: naked option sales, leveraged speculative FX positions, crypto-denominated derivatives, and any instrument requiring settlement infrastructure outside the EEA

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT Summary Return — Modelo 390 (Resumen Anual de IVA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing: minimum fine of EUR 200 plus late-payment surcharges and default interest; material misstatements attract penalties of 50%-150% of the affected amount.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Recapitulative Statement of Intra-Community Transactions — Modelo 349
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 January when intra-EU supplies/acquisitions do not exceed EUR 50,000 in the year; quarterly (30 April, 30 July, 30 October, 30 January) above that threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EUR 40 to EUR 2,000 per omitted or inaccurate item, subject to a minimum of EUR 200 per return, plus default interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Informative Declaration of Third-Party Transactions — Modelo 347
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Telematic filing due by 28 February (or 1 March fallback) following the calendar year; mandatory when aggregate annual transactions with any counterparty exceed EUR 3,005.06
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of EUR 150 per omitted or misstated item (minimum EUR 250), escalating to EUR 6,000 for data relating to transactions exceeding EUR 500,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalization of Official Corporate Books (legalización de libros de actas, registro de socios y libros contables)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after fiscal year-end; by 30 April for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Un-legalized books cannot be tendered as commercial evidence and the Registry may refuse annotations; administrative fine up to approximately EUR 1,200.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary Shareholders' General Meeting approving annual accounts (Junta General Ordinaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting — internal corporate act recorded in the official Minute Book; resolutions later formalized before a notary if required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first six months of each fiscal year; by 30 June for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delayed approval cascades into late deposit of accounts, triggering registry closure (cierre registral); prolonged failure may expose directors to personal liability and constitute grounds for judicial dissolution.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general rate. For tax periods beginning in 2025, qualifying micro-enterprises with net turnover below EUR 1 million generally apply 17% to the first EUR 50,000 of taxable income and 20% to the excess; qualifying entities with turnover of at least EUR 1 million but below EUR 10 million generally apply 24%. Qualifying newly created entities generally apply 15% in the first tax period with a positive taxable base and the following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions. Qualifying start-ups under Law 28/2022 may generally apply 15% for the first tax period with a positive taxable base and the following three periods, subject to eligibility and other conditions. Confirm the applicable rate for the relevant tax period and entity status.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Potential relief includes the reduced rates described above, research and development and technological innovation credits, qualifying audiovisual and other investment credits, and the patent-box regime for qualifying net income from certain intangible assets. Eligibility, limits, documentation, and interaction with other incentives are governed by the Corporate Income Tax Law. No general tax holiday applies to an ordinary online retailer merely because it sells portable power equipment.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward period. Utilization is generally capped at 70% of the pre-loss taxable base, with a minimum offset of EUR 1 million per tax period; statutory exceptions and special rules may apply. The five-year limit in the requested schema does not describe Spanish law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Spanish Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT) e-Office using an accepted electronic certificate or other authorized identification method.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within 25 calendar days following the six months after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the usual filing period is 1–25 July of the following year. Payment may be made by direct debit subject to the AEAT's applicable earlier payment deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the company's legal name, Spanish tax identification number (NIF), registered address, tax period start and end dates, and applicable filing characteristics.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Spanish-resident SL reports its worldwide taxable income, subject to applicable exemptions and relief. A non-resident shareholder does not convert the Spanish SL into a non-resident taxpayer; a foreign entity operating through a Spanish permanent establishment generally uses the applicable non-resident forms instead.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile the statutory accounting profit or loss to the tax base, identifying nondeductible expenses, exempt income, timing differences, and other adjustments required by the Corporate Income Tax Law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include transactions with non-resident related parties at arm's length and retain supporting records. Do not deduct expenses lacking business purpose, adequate evidence, or required withholding compliance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the taxable base after permitted adjustments and apply available tax-loss carryforwards subject to the applicable percentage cap, minimum offset, and anti-abuse restrictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder's own losses cannot be offset against the SL's taxable base. Verify ownership-change and dormant-entity restrictions before using losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the rate applicable to the company's tax period, turnover, and qualifying status; report credits, deductions, and resulting liability using the relevant year's form instructions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The rate is determined by Spanish company-level rules, not the shareholder's residence. Maintain evidence supporting any reduced rate or tax incentive.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Withholdings, payments on account, and balance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit eligible Spanish withholding taxes and installment payments, then calculate the amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only credits legally attributable to the SL and supported by certificates or AEAT records. Shareholder-level foreign tax credits are not entered as company credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete applicable related-party, tax-incentive, loss, and other schedules required by the form for the relevant year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose relevant cross-border related-party transactions and ensure consistency with transfer-pricing documentation, withholding returns, statutory accounts, and any country-by-country or group reporting obligations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without a prior AEAT request may attract a fixed filing penalty, generally reduced where statutory conditions are met; where filing is late after a request or causes a tax loss, penalties may be percentage-based. Late payment generally triggers a surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay during the first 12 months; after 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15%, with late-payment interest also accruing. Tax underpayments may attract penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount, depending on culpability and severity. Exact consequences depend on whether the return is filed voluntarily, the amount due, and the procedural facts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, Corporate Income Tax installment-payment return, filed electronically through the AEAT e-Office.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly installments, generally due in the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December; an applicable direct-debit deadline may be earlier.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File and pay during the applicable 1–20 April, 1–20 October, and 1–20 December periods, subject to the AEAT calendar and payment-method rules. The applicable calculation method depends on statutory requirements and any valid election.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the SL, NIF, tax period, installment period, and calculation method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL files in its own name. A non-resident shareholder does not file this installment return for the SL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the payment using the statutory method applicable to the entity, commonly based on prior-period tax liability or the current-period taxable base where that method is mandatory or elected.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the Spanish statutory calculation and rates; do not substitute the shareholder's home-country tax computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the installment due, payment method, and any permitted credit or adjustment, and retain the electronic filing and payment evidence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use an authorized payment arrangement and ensure the company has access to the AEAT electronic filing system through an authorized representative if necessary.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or missing filing may result in fixed or percentage-based penalties depending on whether tax is due and whether the AEAT has issued a prior request. Late payment generally incurs the statutory surcharge and, where applicable, interest described for Modelo 200; sanctions may also apply for inaccurate or incomplete returns.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The general Spanish withholding tax rate on dividends paid to non-residents is 19%. Domestic exemptions or reduced rates may apply, including the EU Parent-Subsidiary regime for qualifying corporate recipients meeting ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse conditions. A tax treaty may reduce the rate, commonly subject to beneficial ownership and procedural requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's competent tax authority and apply the relevant treaty rate only after verifying entitlement, beneficial ownership, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose-test provisions, and any ownership or holding-period conditions. Provide the certificate and supporting documentation to the Spanish payer for withholding treatment. Where the payer withholds at the domestic rate, the recipient may generally claim a refund through the applicable AEAT procedure, submitting residence and entitlement evidence within the applicable limitation period. Use current AEAT forms and procedures; treaty relief is not automatic solely because a recipient is resident in a treaty country.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The general Spanish non-resident withholding rate on Spanish-source interest and royalties is generally 19%, subject to source rules, exemptions, and treaty relief. Qualifying interest and royalty payments between associated companies in different EU Member States may be exempt under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive as implemented in Spain, subject to qualifying legal form, tax residence and liability, direct ownership, holding-period, beneficial ownership, and anti-abuse conditions. Applicable treaties may reduce rates, often to 0–10% for interest and 0–10% for royalties, but the precise rate depends on the treaty, income classification, recipient status, and entitlement.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Spanish documentation exemptions generally apply to qualifying groups with net turnover below EUR 45 million, subject to statutory exceptions. For transactions with the same related person, documentation is generally not required where the aggregate consideration does not exceed EUR 250,000 at arm's length during the tax period, subject to exclusions and special rules. Spanish Local File and Master File obligations depend on the applicable thresholds and transaction types; country-by-country reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a general standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime of the type used in certain offshore jurisdictions. Spanish tax authorities may nevertheless challenge artificial arrangements under domestic anti-abuse, simulation, conflict-in-application-of-tax-law, permanent-establishment, beneficial-ownership, transfer-pricing, and EU anti-abuse rules. An SL should maintain genuine decision-making, personnel and operational capacity proportionate to its activities, accurate books, commercial evidence, and control over its functions and risks.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate tax evasion and fraudulent returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, fabricating expenses or invoices, maintaining undeclared accounts, or intentionally understating tax due. Criminal tax fraud generally requires the evaded amount to exceed EUR 120,000 for the relevant tax and tax period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax penalties can generally range from 50% to 150% of the tax shortfall, depending on the infringement and aggravating factors. Criminal tax fraud may result in imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded; aggravated cases may carry higher penalties. The tax debt, interest, and civil liability remain separately recoverable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur criminal liability where they personally participate in or authorize the offense. They may also face subsidiary or joint-and-several tax liability in circumstances established by the General Tax Law, including culpable failure to ensure compliance or obstruction of collection. Imprisonment requires criminal conviction; travel bans are not an automatic tax sanction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to account for Spanish VAT on domestic online sales, misclassifying cross-border sales, falsely claiming input VAT, issuing or using fictitious invoices, or failing to apply applicable EU e-commerce and one-stop-shop rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of unpaid VAT, statutory interest, and administrative penalties under the General Tax Law and VAT Law; serious cases may constitute criminal tax fraud when the applicable criminal threshold and intent requirements are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal administrative or criminal liability for their own knowing participation, and statutory derivative tax liability may apply on the facts. Separate civil liability may arise for breach of directors' duties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing misstatement and hidden profit distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing related-party inventory, services, financing, intellectual property, or management charges other than at arm's length; omitting required documentation; or using unsupported charges to shift Spanish profits abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may adjust the taxable base, assess tax and interest, and impose documentation or transfer-pricing penalties under the Corporate Income Tax Law and General Tax Law. Penalty exposure depends on the adjustment, documentation failure, and whether an inaccurate return is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically liable for an adjustment but may incur liability for knowing participation in fraud, fraudulent asset stripping, or statutory grounds for subsidiary or joint-and-several tax liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper withholding and treaty or EU exemption claims
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, or royalties without required withholding, applying treaty or EU exemptions without verifying eligibility, or relying on unsupported residence certificates or beneficial-ownership representations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may be assessed for unwithheld tax, interest, and applicable penalties. Treaty relief or an EU exemption may be denied where entitlement, beneficial ownership, holding-period, or anti-abuse requirements are not met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be exposed where they knowingly authorize non-compliant payments or where statutory grounds for derivative liability are satisfied. Personal criminal liability requires the relevant offense and individual participation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Company dissolution, insolvency, and creditor prejudice
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing assets to shareholders, continuing to incur obligations, or failing to take legally required corporate action while insolvent or when statutory dissolution grounds exist, thereby prejudicing tax authorities or other creditors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential civil liability for damages, insolvency-law consequences, recovery of wrongful distributions, and tax collection measures. Criminal consequences may arise for fraudulent insolvency or related offenses where statutory elements are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal liability under company and insolvency law for breach of duties, failure to act on dissolution grounds, or culpable conduct contributing to insolvency. Liability is fact-specific; piercing the corporate veil is not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering and proceeds of crime
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly concealing, transferring, converting, or using criminal proceeds, or failing to meet applicable customer due diligence, recordkeeping, or suspicious-transaction reporting duties where the SL is a regulated or otherwise covered obliged entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering offenses may result in imprisonment and fines under the Spanish Criminal Code, with penalties depending on the conduct, proceeds, and aggravating circumstances. Administrative sanctions may apply under applicable anti-money-laundering legislation to obliged entities and responsible persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and employees may be criminally liable for knowing participation or legally relevant omission. Corporate criminal liability may also arise where statutory conditions are met. A standard retailer is not automatically an obliged entity solely because it accepts online payments; payment providers have separate regulated obligations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, sham management, and false tax residence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Representing an entity as managed outside Spain despite actual central management in Spain, using nominees to conceal control, claiming treaty benefits through a conduit, or recording fictitious operations to obtain tax advantages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential Spanish tax-residence assessment, denial of treaty or exemption benefits, reassessment of taxable profits, interest, penalties, and, where intentional conduct satisfies criminal elements, prosecution for tax or related offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals may face personal tax, civil, or criminal consequences for their own participation. Corporate separateness is respected absent a legal basis for derivative liability, fraud, abuse, or veil piercing; travel restrictions are not an automatic consequence.
